title.narrative: Protect Lives and Livelihoods of Vulnerable Pastoralist Agro-pastoralist HHs at Risk of La Niña Induced Drought through Anticipatory Action in Borrena Zone , Oromia Region

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed 6-month Anticipatory Action project aims to proactively reduce potential humanitarian challenges, protect livelihoods, and reduce the looming nutrition crisis. This project is aligned with the 2024 second reserve allocation strategy and the national Anticipatory Action framework, complementing the ongoing initiatives in the Borrena Zone, Oromia Region. Considering the anticipated effects of La Niña, the August 2024 post-harvest assessment report indicates that 256,022 individuals will need emergency food assistance through December 2024. Additionally, a proxy Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) rate of 17% has been reported in Eleweye woreda.The situation analysis report from week 28 to 46, of the Borana zone shows 5123 cases of Malaria (out of the total 26252 cases tested) inside the zonal catchment. Gomole, Elwaye and Dillo are found amongest the top five woredas with highest cases of malaria in the zone.While,the report from the Oromia regional agriculture office show recent drought from caused the death of hundreds of thousands of livestock, particularly in southern and southeastern Ethiopia, leaving many pastorals and agropastoral families destitute and in dire need of humanitarian assistance. While the rainfall conditions in these areas improved during 2023 and the first half of 2024, forecasts indicate a high likelihood of drought conditions during the upcoming dry or hageya season-periodically indicating from October to December. These dry conditions are expected to negatively affect livestock production in southern Ethiopia by causing shortages of feed and water, increasing livestock disease outbreaks, prompting abnormal livestock migration, and reducing the market value of animals. ltbrgtTo address this urgent situation, GOAL Ethiopia, in partnership with the local government, has proposed the following anticipatory actions to lessen the impact of these challenges. Rehabilitation of two water schemes utilizing solar power systems for optimal water capture and storage, ensuring safe hygiene practices. It is planned that 17,000 people will gain access to safe and clean drinking water. In addition to this GOAL also plans to address a total of 925 HHs in WASH NFI Items to promote hygiene and sanitation in the woredas. Distribution of drought-tolerant and short-maturing cereal crop seeds, along with farming inputs and mechanized tillage through cash assistance. 440 households will benefit from these interventions. Assistance to 300 pastoralist and agro-pastoralist households through livestock treatment campaigns, animal health services, and supplementary feeds. Establishment and support of 36 Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) and Stabilization Center (SC) sites. Estimated admission of 556 children suffering from Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) to OTP sites, and 52,597 people receiving health consultations and treatments. Screening of 35,070 under-five children and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW) for early identification of acute malnutrition. In addition to the above GOAL will also plan to strengthen the Public health Emergency management of the woredas through provision of training on disease surveillance, early warning system and on Outbreak Management (Prevention and Response) and strengthening the RRT at the woreda level in 03 woredas which are assumed to be malaria prone and have higher probability of epidemics. The total initial budget for the project, which was estimated at $ 650,000 gained an additional cost extension by $195,000. In this context, GOAL proposes a budget of $845,000 to reach around 100,000 people across the three targeted woredas (Gomole, Eleweye, and Dillo). This multi-sectoral approach will incorporate protection mainstreaming, accountability to affected populations (AAP), and the cash-where-possible principlesltbrgtlt/pgt
